items.title: 14.2.2 Deduction of the Important Results (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichhle sabaq mein dot product ki definition aayi: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta\). Ab hum ise sab se saade vectors par chala kar dekhte hain: unit vectors \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\) aur \(\underline{k}\), jo \(x\), \(y\) aur \(z\) axes ki simt mein ek ek unit lambe hain. Yeh chhote se nateeje aage chal kar dot product ka component wala formula banane mein bunyaadi eent (building block) ka kaam karenge, is liye inhein achhi tarah samajh lein.
Kitab kehti hai: dot product ki definition unit vectors \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\) aur \(\underline{k}\) par lagane se humein yeh milta hai:

blocks.alt: Three mutually perpendicular axes through the origin O: z upwards, y to the right and x coming towards the reader. Short arrows along them mark the unit vectors i on the x-axis, j on the y-axis and k on the z-axis.
blocks.caption: Figure: the unit vectors i, j and k along the coordinate axes (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh values kyun aayin? \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\), \(\underline{k}\) unit vectors hain, yani har ek ki magnitude (lambai) \(1\) hai.
(a) mein ek vector ka dot product khud usi ke saath hai. Koi vector apne aap ke saath \(0^{\circ}\) ka angle banata hai, aur \(\cos 0^{\circ} = 1\). Is liye jawab \(1 \times 1 \times 1 = 1\).
(b) mein do alag axes ke unit vectors hain. Axes aapas mein perpendicular (90 darje par) hain, aur \(\cos 90^{\circ} = 0\). Is liye jawab \(1 \times 1 \times 0 = 0\).
Tarteeb (order) badalne se kuch farq nahin parta: \(\underline{j} \cdot \underline{i}\), \(\underline{k} \cdot \underline{j}\) aur \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{k}\) bhi \(0\) hain. Is ki wajah neeche (c) mein hai.

blocks.caption: Unit vectors ki hamari dot-product table (row wala vector dot column wala vector)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Table ko ghor se dekhiye: \(1\) sirf diagonal par hain, baqi sab jagah \(0\). Kyun? Kyun ke diagonal par har vector apne aap se multiply ho raha hai (angle \(0^{\circ}\)), aur baqi jagah do perpendicular vectors (angle \(90^{\circ}\)). Ab batayein \(\underline{k} \cdot \underline{i}\) kya hai? Jawab: \(0\).
Ab teesra nateeja (c). Kitab dikhati hai ke dot product mein vectors ki tarteeb badal dein to jawab nahin badalta:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh commutative property (adla badli ki khoobi) hai: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\) aur \(\underline{v} \cdot \underline{u}\) barabar hain. Kitab \(\underline{v}\) se wapas \(\underline{u}\) ki taraf angle ko \(-\theta\) leti hai. Cosine ek even function hai, yani \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\); is liye jawab wahi rehta hai.
Kyun: aasan alfaaz mein, \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) ke darmiyan angle wahi hai jo \(\underline{v}\) aur \(\underline{u}\) ke darmiyan hai (do sheharon ka faasla dono taraf se ek hi hota hai). Aur \(|\underline{u}||\underline{v}| = |\underline{v}||\underline{u}|\) kyun ke aam numbers ki zarb mein tarteeb se farq nahin parta.
Aage kya kaam aayega? 14.2.5 mein jab hum \((a_{1}\underline{i} + b_{1}\underline{j} + c_{1}\underline{k}) \cdot (a_{2}\underline{i} + b_{2}\underline{j} + c_{2}\underline{k})\) kholenge to nau (9) terms banenge. Unhi terms mein yeh table lagegi: chhe (6) terms zero ho jayenge aur sirf teen bachenge.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Hamari practice, kitab ka sawal nahin.) Numbers ko bahar nikalein, phir table lagayein:
\[(2\underline{i}) \cdot (3\underline{i}) = 6(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i}) = 6\]
\[(2\underline{i}) \cdot (5\underline{j}) = 10(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{j}) = 0\]
\[(4\underline{k}) \cdot (-\underline{k}) = -4(\underline{k} \cdot \underline{k}) = -4\]
Teesre mein dhyan dein: \(\underline{k}\) aur \(-\underline{k}\) bilkul ulti simt mein hain (angle \(180^{\circ}\)), is liye jawab negative aaya.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i} = \underline{j} \cdot \underline{j} = \underline{k} \cdot \underline{k} = 1\), kyun ke angle \(0^{\circ}\) hai.
2. \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{j} = \underline{j} \cdot \underline{k} = \underline{k} \cdot \underline{i} = 0\), kyun ke angle \(90^{\circ}\) hai; tarteeb ulat dein tab bhi \(0\).
3. \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = \underline{v} \cdot \underline{u}\): dot product commutative hai.
4. Yeh table 14.2.5 ke component formula ki bunyaad hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i} = 0\) ya \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{j} = 1\) likh dena. Ulta yaad ho gaya hai! Same vector ho to \(1\), alag vectors hon to \(0\). Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: "apne aap se pura mel (1), perpendicular se koi mel nahin (0)".
2. \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{j} = \underline{k}\) likh dena. Yeh cross product (14.3) ka nateeja hai; dot product ka jawab hamesha number hota hai.
3. \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i}\) ko \(\underline{i}^{2}\) samajh kar \(-1\) likh dena, jaise complex numbers mein \(i^{2} = -1\) tha. Yahan \(\underline{i}\) unit vector hai, iota nahin; \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i} = 1\).
